messages.content:
You are writing for a bank's internal auditor, in UK English.
For each finding, write 2-3 plain sentences: what is wrong, why it matters, what to do.
Use ONLY the numbers given. Do not add, round, combine or calculate numbers.
Do not name customers. Return JSON: {"findings": {"<id>": "<text>", ...}}

{"CV1": "Money order deposits (in) are not monitored at all. 0% monitored: £3,844,620 across 7,722 transactions. No rule can fire on money order deposits (in), so £3,844,620 from 2,020 customers was never checked. Suggested fix: Add scenarios for money order deposits (in), including amount, frequency and split-deposit patterns.", "AD1": "Advisory pattern not caught: Multiple credit card repayments to many individuals. 25 customers match; 4% have a case; £2,115,842. The advisory warns: \"repayments to the credit cards of many different individuals, typically ten or more\". 25 customers match this pattern, but only a transaction-count rule can see them, so only 1 have a case. Assumption: Three‑month window interpreted as 90 days; ten distinct cardholders required; amount range taken from advisory Suggested fix: Add a scenario for: multiple credit card repayments to many individuals (red flag: \"repayments to the credit cards of many different individuals, typically ten or more\").", "AD2": "Advisory pattern not caught: Multiple money orders deposited same day below £2,500. 25 customers match; 4% have a case; £668,454. The advisory warns: \"several money orders on the same day whose combined value is just below £2,500\". 25 customers match this pattern, but no rule can see these transactions, so only 1 have a case. Assumption: ‘Several’ taken as at least 2 money orders; combined total must be <£2,500; repeated on at least 2 separate days Suggested fix: Add a scenario for: multiple money orders deposited same day below £2,500 (red flag: \"several money orders on the same day whose combined value is just below £2,500\").", "BL1": "50 customers with no case look highly unusual. top 50 of 47,056 unflagged customers. These customers never reached the alarm level, but their behaviour is among the most unusual in the bank. Top reasons: 6334452196: money in (£) 831,312 (top 0.1% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 831,312 (top 0.1% of customers); high-risk-country transactions 22 (top 0.5% of customers) | 3781169367: money in (£) 1,016,471 (top 0.1% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 1,016,471 (top 0.1% of customers); high-risk-country transactions 25 (top 0.4% of customers) | 2734005580: money in (£) 839,192 (top 0.1% of customers); money in from abroad (£) 839,192 (top 0.1% of customers); high-risk-country transactions 22 (top 0.5% of customers) Suggested fix: Send these customers for manual review, starting from rank 1.", "BL3": "The valued-client list hides highly unusual customers. 5 of 5 suppressed customers in the top 2% most unusual. These customers are on the valued-client list, so they can never get a case whatever they score, and their behaviour is among the most unusual in the bank. 5 of them have already scored enough for a case. Suggested fix: Remove automatic suppression; review valued clients like anyone else.", "CV2": "Credit card payments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £3,095,313,643. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for credit card payments (out).", "CV3": "Debit card payments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £3,085,585,977. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for debit card payments (out).", "CV4": "Credit card repayments (out) are only checked by a transaction count. only R06_velocity: £63,913,161. The only rule that can fire counts payments; it never looks at amounts, countries or who is being paid. Suggested fix: Add amount and counterparty rules for credit card repayments (out).", "CA1": "Weak rule over-weighted: R01_large_cash. 10 pts, right 1.5% of the time (1-3%, n=529). Cash deposit of £10,000 or more. Only 2% of reviewed customers it flagged were laundering, but it is worth 10 points, so it mostly generates false alarms. Suggested fix: Lower R01_large_cash from 10 to about 1 points to cut false alarms.", "CA2": "Weak rule over-weighted: R04_large_wire. 5 pts, right 4.1% of the time (3-6%, n=999). Wire or cross-border payment of £50,000 or more. Only 4% of reviewed customers it flagged were laundering, but it is worth 5 points, so it mostly generates false alarms. Suggested fix: Lower R04_large_wire from 5 to about 1 points to cut false alarms."}

reply: {"findings":{"CV1":"Money order deposits are not monitored at all – 0% of £3,844,620 across 7,722 transactions from 2,020 customers were checked. This means the full £3,844,620 could contain illicit funds without detection. Add monitoring scenarios for money order deposits, including amount, frequency and split‑deposit patterns.","AD1":"The advisory for multiple credit‑card repayments to many individuals matches 25 customers but only a transaction‑count rule flags one case, leaving £2,115,842 unexamined. This gap risks missing coordinated repayment schemes involving ten or more distinct cardholders within a 90‑day window. Add a scenario that flags multiple credit‑card repayments to many individuals as described.","AD2":"The advisory for several money orders on the same day below £2,500 matches 25 customers yet only one case is flagged, leaving £668,454 unchecked. Without a rule, repeated low‑value money‑order activity can evade detection. Add a scenario for multiple money orders deposited same day below £2,500 as specified.","BL1":"Fifty customers with no case are among the most unusual of 47,056 unflagged customers, each showing money‑in amounts such as £831,312 (top 0.1%) and high‑risk‑country transactions of 22 (top 0.5%). Their extreme profiles could conceal illicit activity despite no alerts. Send these customers for manual review, starting from rank 1.","BL3":"All five suppressed customers in the top 2% most unusual are on the valued‑client list, preventing any case even though five have already scored enough for a case. This exemption hides high‑risk behaviour. Remove automatic suppression and review valued clients like any other customer.","CV2":"Credit‑card payments out are only checked by a transaction‑count rule, covering £3,095,313,643, and ignore amount, country or counterparty details. This limits the ability to spot suspicious high‑value or cross‑border payments. Add amount and counterparty rules for credit‑card payments out.","CV3":"Debit‑card payments out are only checked by a transaction‑count rule, covering £3,085,585,977, without amount, country or counterparty analysis. This reduces detection of risky debit‑card activity. Add amount and counterparty rules for debit‑card payments out.","CV4":"Credit‑card repayments out are only checked by a transaction‑count rule, covering £63,913,161, and do not consider amount, country or payee. This may miss abnormal repayment patterns. Add amount and counterparty rules for credit‑card repayments out.","CA1":"Rule R01_large_cash carries 10 points but is correct only 1.5% of the time (1‑3%, n=529) for cash deposits of £10,000 or more, generating many false alarms. Over‑weighting inflates workload and reduces focus on genuine risk. Lower R01_large_cash from 10 to about 1 point.","CA2":"Rule R04_large_wire carries 5 points but is correct only 4.1% of the time (3‑6%, n=999) for wires of £50,000 or more, leading to frequent false positives. The inflated score wastes investigative resources. Lower R04_large_wire from 5 to about 1 point."}}
